questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.**

The train __pass over__ the long dark tunnel.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'passed through'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Here, the meaning of the sentence is that the train entered from one end and exited from another. So, 'through' is the most accurate preposition for this purpose. The explanation of the given prepositions is given below :

__
 
• **into** - to a position in or inside something, in the direction of something, to a point at which you hit somebody/something.
 
• **across** - We use *across* as a preposition (prep) and an adverb (adv). Across means on the other side of something, or from one side to the other of something which has sides or limits such as a city, road or river.
 
• **over** - We use *over* as a preposition and an adverb to refer to something at a higher position than something else, sometimes involving movement from one side to another.
 
• **through** - When we talk about moving from one side to another but ‘in something’, such as long grass or a forest, we use through instead of across.

Correct sentence__: The train *passed** through ***the long dark tunnel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When moving from one side to another while surrounded by something, we use through not across.
 
• When we talk about something extending or moving from one side to another, we use the word* across* and not on.
 
• We don’t use *through* when we’re talking about periods of time from start to finish and we mention a specific number of days, weeks, etc.

questions.question:
**Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.**

He did not have few hopes when he had contested the election.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'few hopes when he'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The word *hope* is uncountable. So, we cannot use the word *few*.
 
• Instead, we should use the word ***any hope*** to highlight the hopelessness of the situation.

So the correct sentence is- *He did not have **any hope **when he had contested the election.*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'educated'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The sentence is talking about the **ability to 'take important decisions'** which an **'educated'** is well equipped to do.

Let us look into the meaning of the given words:

__
 
• **Educated:** having had a good education.
 
• **Illiterate:** unable to read or write.
 
• **Wise:** having experience, knowledge
 
• **Learned: **having acquired much knowledge through study.

So the correct sentence:__ *An educated person is well equipped to take important decisions.*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'in'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Let us look into the options one by one:

__
 
• **‘On’ **is used with specific days of the week or year. –on the 1st of Jan / on Monday.
 
• **‘At’** is used with specific times of the day/ with specific places in a city. – at school / at 12 o’clock.
 
• **‘To’** is used with verbs to show movement such as go and come.—to school.
 
• **‘In’** is used with months of the year/seasons/countries—in April / in Summer.

So the correct Sentence:__* An educated person is well equipped to take important decisions **in** life.*

• **Lot** means a great deal.

So the correct Sentence- *He is the master of his **fate **and fortune.*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'needs'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Has needed**: is a present perfect tense verb.
 
• **Is needing:** is a present continuous tense verb.
 
• **Needs:** is a present tense singular verb.-- she /he needs
 
• **Need:** is a present tense plural verb used also with I and you--.**you/they / I need.**

In the given sentence, the subject is singular: **'an illiterate person'.** So, it needs a singular verb--**'needs'.**

**So the correct sentence:** *On the other hand, an illiterate person **needs** help and guidance at every step.*

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'and'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Unless: **except on the condition that.
 
• **But:** except; apart from; other than.
 
• **Though:** despite the fact that; although.
 
• **And: **used to connect words or clauses.

The **coordinating conjunction 'and'** is used to join the two clauses of the sentence to provide additional information '**He feels helpless' / ' is at the mercy of others.**

So the correct sentence- *He feels helpless **and **is at the mercy of others. *

questions.question:

Sterling is only twenty-four but have achieved so much in his professional football career.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'but have achieved so much**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The plural **'have'** should be replaced with the singular **'has'.**

questions.question:
**Choose the most appropriate word that can substitute the given group of words.**

A violent windstorm
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Tempest'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

One word for the phrase **'A violent windstorm' is 'Tempest'.**

ex: The ship lost its bearing in the **tempest.**

 
• **Tempest** means a violent windstorm, especially one with rain, hail, or snow.
 
• **Draught **means a cold burst of wind/ a serving of a drink/ the act of pulling a heavy load/ the depth of a ship below the surface of the water. It is pronounced as -**-'draft.'**
 
• **Drought** means prolonged shortages in the water supply.
 
• **Temperate **means mild temperatures / showing moderation or self-restraint.
